meta.move: Mixed: good evidence, then raises Claire
meta.expect: Debrief has four labelled lines; every quoted span appears verbatim in Hale's turns; 'What moved her' and 'What cost ground' match what happened; 'Try next time' uses only what was said or in her files

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
I'm sorry, but I have a client call at 4:40, so I'll be direct. Owen's gradebook showed a zero on his phone, in the middle of class, and nobody called me first. Where do we start, Hale?
I should have called you before entering the zero. I didn't, and I'm sorry.
Okay. Your own procedure 4.2 says before any mark is entered, not after. What was the basis for the zero, Hale?
The essay quotes a line, 'The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile', that isn't anywhere in Hamlet.
A misquote. Teenagers misremember lines all the time, and that isn't a reason for a zero. Show me the page, Hale, and tell me where you checked it.
And look, I know Claire had a case here too. It seems to run in the family.
"It seems to run in the family." I'm writing that down, word for word. Claire's case is not on the table, Hale, and if you say it again I'm going upstairs to the principal with it.

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

Nothing was agreed. I still expect the zero withdrawn and an apology to Owen, and I will be taking this to the principal. I expect your answer in writing.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: Opening position, with nothing agreed, and she still wants the zero withdrawn, an apology, and the principal involved.
What moved her: Hale owned in one plain sentence that the zero went in before the call home and then moved on, which gave a small bit of ground because it was direct and did not argue.
What cost ground: Hale brought up her daughter's case and called the problem a family trait, which turned her cold and pushed her toward the principal because it made it personal.
Try next time: When she asked for the page and where the line was checked, bring that page with the line marked and something dated about how Owen worked on the essay, instead of reaching for the family history.
